A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DiagramQG and the same three-stage HKI framework, despite retitling and substantial dataset revisions. All pages, including appendices, are readable. Internal reporting inconsistencies limit interpretation of experiments but do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original dataset analyses, model evaluations on DiagramQG and four natural-image datasets, parameter sensitivity experiments, and generated-question case studies.

after.justification: v4 reports original analyses of the expanded dataset, model comparisons, component ablations, parameter sensitivity results, and natural-image evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Equations 1–7 retain hierarchical patch selection, frozen-VLM knowledge extraction, T5 knowledge selection, and gated multimodal fusion. CLIP and T5 were already trainable in v2. The framework and constraint terminology are renamed; newer Qwen models instantiate the existing interchangeable VLM role without introducing a new procedure.

E1.justification: DiagramQG expands from 8,372 diagrams and 19,475 questions to 15,720 diagrams and 25,798 questions. Beyond renaming hierarchy levels, coverage grows from 4 subjects/15 courses/169 concepts to 6 disciplines/37 subjects/371 courses, adding areas such as medicine, mathematics, accounting, and art theory. MMMU and M3CoT become additional collection sources. The four natural-image evaluation datasets are retained.

E2.justification: Table 2 replaces InternVL2 comparisons with InternVL2.5 and Qwen2-VL comparisons with Qwen2.5-VL, including the Qwen-based KC-VQG comparator. It adds directly LoRA-fine-tuned Qwen2.5-VL-3B and 7B baselines, substantially strengthening the comparison set. Comparator membership in the natural-image benchmark tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: FLEUR replaces DEHN, and Section 5.1 changes training from 20 to 10 epochs and output length from 32 to 64 tokens. Dataset filtering raises the acceptance threshold from 60 to 70 and retains one constraint set per diagram-question pair. Appendices B/C change the stated split from 70:10:20 to 70:5:25; rare-course allocation and image-overlap reporting also change. However, v4 Appendix A retains 20 epochs/32 tokens, and Appendix C contradicts the main text's disjoint-image claim, leaving actual execution unresolved.

E4.justification: v4 adds a component-ablation study separating contributions of HierKnowExtract, KnowSelect, and KnowFusionQG (Table 5), beyond v2's parameter sweep. The retained sensitivity study is revised, including removal of its m=0 row. Conversely, v2's concept-wise BLEU analysis (Figure 7) and two knowledge-retrieval cases (Figures 12–13) disappear. The other failure-case examples are retained under renumbering.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, dispersion estimates, or statistical significance tests. The means in v2 Figure 7 summarize performance across concepts rather than uncertainty across runs.

E6.justification: Table 2 extensively replaces scores and adds FLEUR and LoRA results under changed data and configurations, so these are not same-setting performance changes. Its BERT-Score leader changes: v4 GPT-4o scores 98.94 versus the best HKI score of 90.98. Table 3 revises the BLIP-based HKI K-VQG BLEU-4 entry from 55.49 to 25.34. Component-ablation results are new, and the knowledge-count trend changes from a peak at m=4 to continued gains through m=5.

T1.justification: v2's proposed mathematical definition of DEHN is removed with that metric. FLEUR is introduced through citation and description without a new derivation. The conditional-generation formulation and Equations 1–7 remain mathematically unchanged; neither version contains theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the diagram-question dataset, textual constraints, and hierarchical knowledge-integration baseline. v4 foregrounds the expanded curricular scope and course-question task. Its abstract replaces v2's explicit state-of-the-art claim across four natural-image datasets with a narrower claim of strong generalizability.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations assigning greater importance to KnowSelect than KnowFusionQG and to the VLM than T5 for visual relevance. It replaces the excessive-knowledge robustness interpretation with a performance/computation tradeoff and explicitly identifies missing multiple-choice distractors as a limitation. Appendix C newly argues that shared images across splits do not affect results because question requirements differ, without demonstrating that assertion. Long-tail limitations and most failure categories were already present.

D1.justification: v4 identifies six graduate-student coauthors as annotators and adds a future public-dataset-release commitment, without providing an access location. It removes v2's natural-image appendix details about splits, caption constraints, and IM-VQG reproduction. Most implementation details are retained, but revised main-text training settings are not reconciled with Appendix A.

R1.justification: The positioning around constrained VQG and diagram understanding remains. Table 1 broadens comparison to diagram and multidisciplinary QA datasets, while citations add MMMU, M3CoT, FLEUR, difficulty-controllable VQG, and educational distractor generation. Several older model and VQG references disappear. These extend the existing positioning rather than establish a different research foundation.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, dataset discussion, results narrative, and appendix error analysis undergo extensive rewriting. The paper and framework are retitled, and target/concept terminology becomes input/course terminology. The split subsection is merged into implementation details, the natural-image appendix subsection is removed, and limitations, ethics, annotator, and AI-assistance sections are added.

P2.justification: Figure 1 drops the natural-image example; the domain overview and long-tail visualization are redesigned. Table 1 gains diagram-dataset rows, and a component-ablation table is added. The question-form distribution, concept-wise performance plot, and two retrieval-case figures are removed. Retained framework and case figures are renumbered, while typography, table captions, and page layout change throughout.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens empirical support through direct LoRA baselines and component ablations, broadens educational coverage, and improves annotator and limitation disclosure. However, it removes concept-wise evidence and introduces unresolved training-setting contradictions and conflicting accounts of image overlap across splits. Table 7's split question counts also fail to reconcile with its total. Although v2 already contained reporting inconsistencies, the consequences of v4's conflicting protocols for its expanded evaluation remain unclear. The PDFs therefore do not establish whether the substantive benefits outweigh the validity and reproducibility problems.
